stories.title: Punjab govt to ban 'spying objects' equipped with hidden cameras, recording devices
summary: The Punjab government decided on Monday to ban objects equipped with hidden cameras and recording devices, including pens, eyeglasses and watches.

The statement said “strict legal action” would be taken against the use, purchase and sale of “spying devices and covert electronic devices”, further warning that the “illegal use” of objects equipped with hidden cameras would result in “severe penalties”.
Taking up the plea on Thursday, the LHC directed the federal government to forward a summary to the federal cabinet regarding the unregulated import and sale of smart glasses.

stories.title: CDF Munir, new Saudi envoy express satisfaction at progress made under Makkah pact: ISPR
summary: CDF Munir congratulated the ambassador on his appointment and expressed confidence that his tenure would further strengthen the longstanding fraternal ties between Islamabad and Riyadh, which are “rooted in shared faith, mutual trust and strategic partnership”.
DPM Dar, meanwhile, underscored longstanding fraternal and strategic ties between Islamabad and Riyadh when he met Albugamy.

Islamabad and Riyadh have signed two defence pacts aimed at collective deterrence, the Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement between the two and the Makkah Joint Defence Alliance that also includes Turkiye.

stories.title: 'We never gave up': Naqvi highlights Pakistan's peace efforts in US-Iran war at Qatar forum
summary: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Monday highlighted Pakistan’s mediation efforts between the United States and Iran, affirming that Islamabad “never gave up”.

Naqvi, who has been involved in Islamabad’s peace efforts and has made several trips to Iran since the war began, said: “There were moments when the situation was extremely tense, but we never gave up. “We continued talking, listening and working to build trust.
CDF Munir, accompanied by Naqvi, had visited Iran in August “as part of Pakistan’s efforts to promote regional peace and stability”.

stories.title: PPP was the 'last party' in favour of governor's rule in KP, says Sharjeel
summary: Senior Sindh Minister Sharjeel Inam Memon on Monday asserted that the PPP was the “last party” in favour of governor’s rule and emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, saying that it had emphasised dialogue as the first course of action.
The Centre imposed governor’s rule and emergency in KP on Oct 11, citing the provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism.
Coming to his party’s involvement in the imposition of governor’s rule in KP, he said the PPP was the “last party” in favour of the move.

stories.title: SOCIETY: BALOCHISTAN’S UNENDING CYCLES OF POVERTY
summary: Some even work for food | Photo by Zaheer Baloch Mian Dad has spent much of his life ploughing fields on a tractor.

Debt, unequal sharecropping arrangements and climate shocks can trap entire families in a vicious cycle of dependence THE BOTTOM RUNG Mian’s situation is not unusual in a province where poverty remains widespread.
RESETTING THE CLOCK The 2022 floods that pushed Mian Dad into debt were not the first to disrupt the relationship between landlords and agricultural workers in Nasirabad.

stories.title: Climate exodus
summary: SOUTH Asia may see a vast movement of people as climate change makes parts of the region harder to live in.
An influx of climate-displaced families could deepen these problems.
The challenge is to ensure that people forced to move by climate change can rebuild their lives.

stories.title: Kremlin says Putin, Trump and Xi could hold a three-way meeting in China next month
summary: The Kremlin said on Monday that Russian President Vladimir Putin, US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping could hold a three-way meeting on the sidelines of next month’s APEC summit in China and that a potential meeting had come up in talks.
Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha criticised the idea of such a summit. “A trilateral meeting between the leaders of Ukraine, the US, and Russia could help end the war sooner.
A trilateral meeting between the leaders of Russia, China, and the US would do only the opposite: encourage Putin to continue this war,” he said on X.

stories.title: SHC dismisses state appeal against Mahrang's 2025 acquittal in sedition case
summary: The Sindh High Court (SHC) on Monday dismissed an appeal filed by the provincial government through the prosecutor general against the acquittal of Baloch Yakjehti Committee (BYC) leader Mahrang Baloch in a sedition case, declaring it non-maintainable.
The prosecution claimed that the ATC had ignored facts while accepting Mahrang’s acquittal application.
Mahrang, who is in Quetta prison in connection with other cases, had filed an acquittal application under Section 265-K of the Code of Criminal Procedure before ATC-V, which the court allowed.

stories.title: French prime minister calls for curfews as govt grapples with unrest
summary: Saturday’s demonstrations saw some half a million people turn out across France to protest the cost of living, but morphed into some of the worst violence to rock the country in years, with town halls and shops looted and set ablaze.
French President Emmanuel Macron also refused Interior Minister Laurent Nunez’s resignation even as he acknowledged security and intelligence failures in the government response.

More than 2,000 shops were expected to have been affected by the weekend’s violence across France, with damage running into “hundreds of millions of euros”, according to chamber of commerce president Alain Di Crescenzo.

stories.title: IHC takes up Imaan, Hadi’s appeals against framing of charges in security breach case
summary: Justice Minhas questioned whether the proceedings could not be conducted through a video link, observing that the accused had been connected through the facility and that their attendance had been recorded when the charges were framed.

Azad reiterated that the appeals also challenged the inclusion of anti-terrorism provisions in the case and repeatedly urged the high court to halt the trial. “We shall see; we will let you know,” Justice Minhas remarked.
ATC hearing adjourned Meanwhile, ATC Judge Tahir Abbas Sipra conducted the proceedings of the security breach case against Imaan and Hadi at the Adiala jail, where they are incarcerated.

stories.title: Pakistan providing 'whatever support' Saudi Arabia needs for its defence: DG ISPR
summary: Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry has said Pakistan is providing “whatever support is needed” to defend Saudi Arabia amid attacks by Yemen’s Houthi rebels against the kingdom.

On whether Pakistan’s support to Saudi Arabia will strictly remain defensive if the Houthi attacks continue, the the military spokesperson said all three members of the alliance were “absolutely clear […] that this alliance has no offensive intent; it is purely defensive”.
Earlier this month, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye convened an emergency meeting under the Makkah Defence Alliance and agreed to deploy military forces and capabilities rapidly in the kingdom.

stories.title: TV anchor Iqrarul Hassan sent to Karachi prison on judicial remand in Peca case
summary: KARACHI: A judicial magistrate on Monday sent anchorperson Iqrarul Hassan to prison on an eight-day judicial remand until Oct 26 in a cybercrime case pertaining to the alleged dissemination of anti-state content.
Hassan was arrested a week ago for allegedly disseminating anti-state, false and defamatory content on his official social media accounts.
On Monday, Hassan was presented before Karachi (East) Judicial Magistrate-I Judge Gulraiz Memon upon the completion of his six-day physical remand.

stories.title: Musk says will give SpaceX share to 'every kid in America'
summary: There are around 73 million children under the age of 18 in the United States, according to 2024 data from the US Census Bureau.
Musk owns 38 per cent of SpaceX, according to Forbes.
The company’s Starship megarocket reached orbit for the first time in September, a milestone for the rocket central to Musk’s Mars ambitions.

stories.title: Army major martyred, 4 terrorists killed in Balochistan IBOs: ISPR
summary: In the first operation on October 18, security forces conducted an IBO in the general area of Jattakabad, during which four terrorists were eliminated. “A large cache of arms and ammunition was also recovered,” it added.
In the second operation, ISPR added that security forces conducted a series of clearance operations in the general area of Shadi Kaur, Pasni, in Gwadar.
A day earlier, security forces killed eight “India-sponsored” terrorists during IBOs conducted in the Quetta, Nushki and Khuzdar districts of Balochistan.

stories.title: Kidnapping, torture case registered against railway police officials amid dispute with KMC over road project
summary: The development comes amid a dispute between Pakistan Railways (PR) police and KMC City Wardens over a road project aimed at easing traffic congestion in the city.

According to the FIR, Imran said a road had been under construction from Natha Khan to Pehlwan Goth for the past four months and that he was on traffic management duty at the site on the day of the incident.
The incident unfolded on Sunday afternoon when railway police officials intervened at the construction site and stopped the work, prompting the chief of KMC City Wardens to arrive at the site.

stories.title: We were ready with our tax filings, was the FBR?
summary: In other words, although the taxpayer’s statutory deadline remained September 30, the final return itself arrived when nearly two-thirds of the presumed compliance period had already vanished.
The statutory deadline remained September 30, but taxpayers and practitioners were effectively given certainty about the final prescribed electronic return only when September had already begun.
More importantly, the law itself should guarantee a minimum effective compliance period — say ninety days — beginning only when the final prescribed electronic return is fully operational.

stories.title: UN agency to end monthly aid to 500,000 people in Gaza over funding shortfall
summary: With the cutbacks, 1.1 million Palestinians in Gaza — still about half the population — will be receiving either food or cash assistance each month from the UN agency, in reduced amounts.

The World Food Programme (WFP) said its efforts had mitigated the effects during a famine last year in Gaza and warned that conditions had not improved to the point that it can take away aid. “People are not safe.
According to the latest assessments, 1.4 million people — or two-thirds of Gaza’s population — are still “acutely food insecure” and need humanitarian assistance to survive, he said.

stories.title: Covering Karachi's Nehr-i-Khayyam poses risk of urban flooding: experts
summary: She also demanded an environmental impact assessment (EIA) and said residents should be informed about the project.
Why is it necessary to cover everything with cement?” He warned that the waterway had helped prevent rainwater from accumulating during heavy rainfall in the area.

In a press statement, residents of the area demanded the suspension of construction until the required environmental assessment had been conducted and approval obtained from the Sindh Environmental Protection Agency.

stories.title: Pakistan face stern England test
summary: Pakistan will look to build on their solid performance in the opening match when they take on England in the second show of the ODI tri-series at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on Tuesday (today)).
Led by Shaheen Shah Afridi, Pakistan made a bright start to the series on Sunday, making a strong comeback to beat Sri Lanka by 37 runs.
A major boost for England is the return of premier leg-spinner Adil Rashid, who has rejoined the squad after a hand injury ruled him out of their recent 2-1 ODI series victory over Sri Lanka.

stories.title: Shastri urges India to use Bumrah sparingly ahead of ODI World Cup
summary: India should keep Jasprit Bumrah fresh for next year's one-day international World Cup by selecting him mainly for test cricket and using the pace spearhead sparingly in ‌other formats, former coach Ravi Shastri said.
Bumrah was recalled to India's test squad for their two-match series in New Zealand last week, but will not play in the five ODIs and five Twenty20 internationals that precede the tests.

Then he should be used sparingly in the other formats." Following their tour ⁠of New Zealand, India will host Sri Lanka and Zimbabwe in limited-overs series, before hosting Australia in a five-test series ⁠which concludes in February.

stories.title: Atif Aslam celebrates wife with heartfelt 'Happy Sarah Day' Instagram post
summary: Singer Atif Aslam celebrated his wife Sarah Bharwana’s birthday with an affectionate message on Instagram, saying one day was not enough to honour the woman he calls his queen.
Known for his soulful voice and romantic songs, Aslam has occasionally shared affectionate messages for Sarah on social media.
In a March anniversary-related post, the singer shared a loving message about wishing he had met her sooner so they could have made even more memories together.

stories.title: Traffic accident on Multan’s Bosan Road kills 5 men in their 20s
summary: A road accident on Multan’s Bosan Road claimed the lives of five men in their 20s early on Monday after their speeding Toyota Corolla hit a road divider before crashing into the wall of a nearby plot and catching fire, Rescue 1122 said.
Rescue 1122 identified three of the five victims as men aged 22, 23 and 28.
All five victims had sustained head injuries, Rescue 1122 said.

stories.title: Tiger Shroff's car targeted in Mumbai shooting, three arrested
summary: Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff’s BMW was targeted in a shooting outside filmmaker Rohit Shetty’s residence in Mumbai’s Juhu area on Sunday evening, with the actor subsequently rushing his injured driver to hospital.
Shroff reportedly took the wheel after the shooting and drove to Santacruz Police Station before being escorted by police to Nanavati Hospital to ensure his driver received medical attention.
According to The Statesman, the Lawrence Bishnoi gang claimed responsibility for the shooting.

stories.title: Karachi to remain hot and dry as temperatures near 39°C: Met Office
summary: Karachi is expected to experience hot and dry weather over the coming days, with maximum temperatures likely to reach 39 degrees Celsius, the Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) said on Monday.

Deputy Director of the Met Department in Karachi Anjum Nazir Zaigham said hot and dry conditions were likely to continue over the next few days, with maritime winds and north-westerly winds from Balochistan expected to influence weather conditions.

Also Read: Karachi city sizzles past nine-year September heat record Cooler mornings and nights were expected to begin from mid-November, while colder weather was likely to set in between early and mid-December, Zaigham said.

stories.title: Victoria Falls Stadium nears completion
summary: Zimbabwe’s preparations for the 2027 ICC Men’s Cricket World Cup are progressing, with the new Mosi-oa-Tunya International Cricket Stadium in Victoria Falls nearing completion ahead of its planned debut at the global tournament.
Zimbabwe will co-host the tournament with South Africa and Namibia, with Harare, Bulawayo and Victoria Falls among the destinations set to welcome teams and supporters.
Selected stands at Harare Sports Club and Queens Sports Club will receive bucket seats, while floodlights are planned for Queens Sports Club and the Victoria Falls stadium ahead of the tournament.

stories.title: Oil-rich Alberta vote to determine next step towards possible separation from Canada
summary: Alberta decides Monday if it wants to pursue a binding referendum on leaving Canada, with Prime Minister Mark Carney warning a separatist win would bring dangerous uncertainty during a trade war with the United States.

AI influence Monday’s referendum features 10 questions, including several related to immigration, but focus is on question 10, which asks: “Should Alberta remain a province of Canada?” or should the province take the legal steps required for a definitive independence vote?

After a separatist party won Quebec’s provincial election on October 5, tech billionaire Elon Musk posted that “they would be better off” if they seceded. “Alberta and Saskatchewan should separate too,” he added.

stories.title: Wiegman signs England contract extension
summary: England women's head coach Sarina Wiegman has signed a two-year contract extension taking her through until the end of the 2029 women's European Championship, the Football Association announced Monday.
Wiegman has led England to tournament triumphs at both the 2022 and 2025 Euros, as well as a first World Cup final in 2023, since taking charge in September 2021.
England, beaten by Spain in the 2023 World Cup final in Australia, will face Ukraine over a two-legged play-off in November and December for a place in next year's tournament in Brazil.

stories.title: Massive fire breaks out at garment factory warehouse in Karachi's SITE area
summary: A massive fire broke out at a warehouse of a garments factory near Metroville in Karachi’s SITE area on Monday, prompting the deployment of fire and rescue teams, according to the Karachi Metropolitan Corporation (KMC) and Sindh Rescue 1122.
Meanwhile, fire brigade officials at the site told The Express Tribune that they were facing difficulties due to a "shortage of water".
"More than five fire tenders from Rescue 1122 and the Karachi Metropolitan Corporation (KMC) Fire Brigade reached the scene to take part in the firefighting operation," the spokesperson had said.

stories.title: French PM calls for 'partial curfews' in cities hit by riots and looting
summary: Interior Minister Laurent Nunez earlier admitted that police had "lost control" of the protests in several cities, while the Yellow Vest movement called for a new round of protests on Saturday.

Meanwhile, French President Emmanuel Macron rejected the resignation of Interior Minister Nunez following widespread violence and looting across the country during last weekend's protests, according to broadcaster BFMTV.

Students block access to Louvre Museum in support of high school protests Students blocked access to the Louvre Museum in Paris on Monday in support of ongoing high school protests and to denounce what they described as police repression, the French media reported.

stories.title: Ex-lawmaker from Bajaur declines to be part of KP ARDC
summary: Mr Khan, who remained a two-time MNA from Bajaur, however, did not cite the reason for refusing to be part of the planned council, which will be headed by former Khyber Pakhtunkhwa governor Eng Shaukatullah Khan, who also belongs to Bajaur district.

Development Council members from Khyber express ignorance about their role Meanwhile, Ittehad-i-Malkanan Bajaur, an alliance of elders, on Sunday rejected the ARDC, saying the alliance wasn’t consulted on the council’s formation.

The five members selected from Khyber also expressed their lack of knowledge about the selection criteria for council members, with some of the local elders declining the offer when they were approached by the district administration.

stories.title: Four terrorists held, hideouts destroyed in KP's Lakki operation
summary: LAKKI MARWAT: Four terrorists were arrested, and their hideouts were destroyed during a search and strike operation in Lakki Marwat district on Sunday.

stories.title: Police allegedly arrest PTI MNA Nasim Ali Shah from Bannu
summary: The arrest came amid a wider crackdown on PTI leaders and workers in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) following the imposition of governor’s rule and a state of emergency in the province on October 11.

Non-functional chief minister Sohail Afridi, PTI provincial president Junaid Akbar and K-P Assembly Speaker Babar Saleem Swati were among the senior party figures taken into protective custody following the federal government’s intervention.

According to a petition filed by Sohail Afridi’s brother, Muhammad Aamir, in the Peshawar High Court (PHC), the former K-P chief minister was allegedly taken from the Chief Minister’s House in Peshawar on October 11 by armed, masked men in the presence of the city’s police chief.

stories.title: Climate-smart farming for rice growers to reduce water use discussed in Gujranwala consultation
summary: LAHORE: In a bid to slash agricultural water consumption by nearly a third and cut methane emissions almost by half, the rice sector is moving to adopt climate-smart farming techniques that can allow local growers to unlock lucrative international carbon markets.

At the core of the proposed transformation is the alternate wetting and drying (AWD), a precise water-management method where rice fields undergo controlled periods of drying rather than continuous flooding.

stories.title: Livestock card scheme behind 43pc rise in animal exports, claims Punjab govt
summary: LAHORE: Punjab’s livestock sector has recorded a 43pc increase in animal exports, with 400,000 animals prepared for export in a year and rural livestock farmers expected to earn Rs11 billion.

This was claimed by the government in a press release attributing the success to the Chief Minister’s Punjab Livestock Card Scheme launched by her under which farmers are receiving Rs27,000 per animal to meet feed and fodder expenses.
Under the Livestock Connect system, the government has established direct links with 1,725 fattening farms, 20 export slaughterhouses, 88 meat exporters and 34 meat traders.

stories.title: Tensions in Gulab Devi Lahore after patient’s death, brawl between attendants, doctors
summary: LAHORE: Tensions spiked in the Gulab Devi Hospital when a young male patient died soon after a physical clash between his female relatives and a lady doctor in the hospital.
Later, the male colleagues of the lady doctor claimed that she had turned towards one of the female attendants to stop her from recording her video.
They also lashed out at the police for use of excessive force for arresting and sending female attendants behind the bars at a time when their patient was in need of critical care.

stories.title: Questions raised over Islamabad's Pims doctors’ absorption process
summary: ISLAMABAD: Questions have been raised over the Ministry of Health’s handling of the absorption of doctors at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims).

Doctors urge health ministry to implement SC judgement without discrimination “The ministry had proposed that such doctors should either be absorbed in Pims at the bottom of the existing seniority list or returned to their parent institutions,” he claimed.
Doctors have urged the ministry to implement the Supreme Court judgement transparently and without discrimination, particularly in the wake of the recent Pims fire tragedy.

stories.title: Two injured as MNA’s son allegedly jumps red light in Islamabad
summary: Meanwhile, a Corolla Altis bearing registration plate GAW-308, driven by the suspect, approached from the E-7 side of Margalla Road at high speed.
The car allegedly jumped the red light and hit the motorcycle as the two-wheeler was crossing Margalla Road.
The FIR stated that the suspect drove the car rashly and at high speed, violated the traffic signal and hit the complainant and his colleague.

stories.title: SC sets up legal aid cell for deserving litigants
summary: The Supreme Court on Monday established a Legal Aid Cell at its Public Facilitation Centre (PFC) to assist deserving litigants seeking guidance in pursuing or defending their legal rights.

The court has also introduced the 1818 helpline through which members of the public can obtain information about their cases, seek assistance in using online services and raise administrative queries.

She said the broader objective was to organise administrative, technological and legal assistance around the needs of citizens rather than requiring litigants to navigate the court system on their own.

stories.title: Imaan, Hadi seek suspension of ATC trial over alleged procedural violations during indictment
summary: The defence on Monday urged the Islamabad High Court (IHC) to halt trial proceedings against lawyer Imaan Mazari and Hadi Ali Chatha, alleging procedural violations in the framing of charges and arguing that the accused had not been physically present when they were indicted.

The court was hearing appeals filed by Imaan and Hadi against the anti-terrorism court's (ATC) dismissal of their applications challenging their indictment and the terrorism charges in a case related to the removal of barriers.

Justice Inam asked whether the lawyers had received copies of the relevant documents. “Copies have not been provided,” State Ali Azad told the court, adding that he wanted to examine how the indictment had been framed.

stories.title: Kremlin dismisses allegations of Russia's involvement in Europe unrest
summary: No one is taking seriously "absurd accusations" of Russia's involvement in unrest in Europe, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on Monday.

Also Read: Macron rejects interior minister's resignation after France-wide riots Peskov also said that Russian President Vladimir Putin had backed proposals by Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin for a reshuffle in the government.
Asked whether Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi was expected to visit Russia by the end of this year or in 2027, Peskov said the visit would most likely take place next year.
